A simple and effective method to check for the presence of a non-dispersed sticky layer, often referred to as a cake, is by probing the bottom of the container with a glass rod or a similar device that is appropriately sized for the container. If the formulation has flocculated, it may not be possible to re-disperse this sticky layer. 2. Analytical methods used must comply with standards such as CIPAC, AOAC, or equivalent. If these methods have not yet been published, the proposer must submit full details, including appropriate method validation data, to FAO/WHO. 3. Separate clauses must be provided for each relevant impurity. Clauses addressing the content of free active ingredients and the release rate of active ingredients are required only for encapsulated active ingredients and only if relevant to the intended properties of the capsules. 4. A clause to control the release rate is typically required for capsules designed to exhibit slow or controlled-release properties. Similarly, a clause to control free active ingredients is usually necessary when encapsulation is intended to regulate the release or stability of the active ingredient or to reduce the risk of accidental exposure to users. 5. If multiple active ingredients are encapsulated, specific limits must be provided for each. Methods for determining free active ingredients and release rates may be product-specific. 6. Homogenization must be performed carefully to prevent aeration of the sample. If the buyer requires results in both g/kg and g/L at 20°C, in case of disputes, the analytical results should be calculated as g/kg. 7. Only relevant impurities should be included in the clause, and it should be omitted if there are none. Analytical methods must be peer-validated. 8. Percentages may be specified in one or more ranges, as appropriate for the product. Laser diffraction is not always suitable for measuring the particle size distribution of liquid formulations. 9. Dispersion stability tests should be conducted at a 2% dilution or, alternatively, at the highest and lowest recommended rates of use. Oversized capsules, crystals, agglomerates, or extraneous materials that could block spray nozzles or filters in the spray tank must be avoided. 10. The mass of the sample used in testing should correspond to the maximum application concentration recommended by the supplier. Tests should be conducted in CIPAC standard water D. 11. After manufacturing and during shipping, it is often impossible for buyers or sellers to guarantee that the formulation has not been exposed to freezing temperatures. Freezing of a ZE formulation may result in undesirable, irreversible changes, such as capsule failure due to crystallization of the active ingredient. Therefore, the ability of the formulation to withstand repeated freeze-thaw cycles is a critical property. 12. Freeze-thaw stability tests should be conducted at temperatures of 20 ± 2°C and -10 ± 2°C, using 18-hour freeze and 6-hour melt cycles for a total of four cycles, unless otherwise specified. 13. Samples of the formulation taken before and after the storage stability test should be analyzed concurrently to minimize analytical error. 14. ZE formulations are mixed formulations of CS and SE, consisting of microcapsules, solid fine particles, and emulsion droplets, each containing one or more active ingredients. These formulations are intended for dilution in water prior to spray application. 15. Formulating active ingredients together eliminates the need for tank mixing, which can lead to incompatibility, and facilitates control of a broader range of pests with fewer applications. ZE formulations are easy to handle, measure, dust-free, non-flammable, and exhibit good miscibility with water. 16. Encapsulation of one or more active ingredients serves various purposes, such as increasing residual biological activity, reducing acute toxicity, or achieving a physically or chemically stable water-based formulation. The purpose determines whether free active ingredient content and release rate are relevant properties for a specific product. 17. Mixed formulations of CS and SE are not indefinitely stable, and it is essential to ensure that the formulation remains suitable for use after transportation and storage. Quantification of parameters such as active ingredient content (total, free, and release rate), pourability, dispersion stability, and wet sieve tests is necessary, particularly after high and low-temperature stability tests. 18. For mosquito coils, the material must burn without producing a flame, except at the beginning, and should be easily extinguishable after ignition. The average weight of coils must not deviate by more than ±10% from the declared weight when determined on 20 single coils. 19. The average burning time of mosquito coils, determined from five single coils burning continuously in a draft-free atmosphere, must not be less than the declared time. Coils must withstand a minimum load of 120 g without breaking, and twin coils must be designed for easy separation, with no more than three coils breaking out of 50 separated twin coils. 20. Sampling procedures must ensure that samples are stored to prevent material deterioration, sampling instruments are clean and dry, and samples are protected against contamination. Random sampling methods, such as using random number tables, should be employed to ensure unbiased selection. 21. Test samples must be prepared by selecting sufficient quantities of twin-form coils at random from individual boxes. These samples should be packed and labeled according to general requirements. 22. Analytical methods for testing must comply with CIPAC or AOAC standards. If unpublished methods are used, full details and validation data must be submitted to WHO. 23. The water content of mosquito coils should not exceed 120 g/kg. The average weight per coil is typically 12 g, ensuring a burning time approximately equivalent to the normal duration of sleep. In special circumstances, the burning time may be adjusted as stated on the label. 24. The breaking load or tensile strength of mosquito coils must be determined using validated methods to ensure product durability.
